_about: Pinned hashes and known gate failures. Machine-editable by --rebaseline. History in tests/BASELINE.md. READ THIS BEFORE CHASING A HASH: determinismHash and the smoke tables are CHANGE DETECTORS, not the determinism invariant. The invariant is that the same seed+tick+inputs reproduce bit-identically, and the determinism gate tests that separately (twice-run comparison) -- it keeps passing while these values move. All we require is determinism; new numbers are fine. An intentional change to hashed state (a reaction chance, a material, a sim.* value, a re-baked asset) ALWAYS moves them: run --selftest --rebaseline, commit the new values with the change, and move on. Do not investigate an expected move, do not try to restore the old number, and do not call it a broken sim. Only an UNEXPECTED move is a finding.
_recorded_at: 46b7ec7 2026-08-21, RTX 3060 Ti; last re-recorded 2026-08-25 for the GAS VERTICAL MODEL (buoyancy as a redistributable probability)
_treeAtlas_about: tree-atlas gate. treeAtlasHash is FNV-1a over the uploaded atlas buffer (assets/trees/*.svtree, remapped to engine material ids). It moves when a species is re-baked -- which also moves determinismHash, so this is what names WHICH asset did it instead of leaving a world-hash diff with no cause attached. Re-bake with node scripts/bake_trees.mjs, then --selftest --rebaseline.
_scale_about: scale gate. scaleMetres_<def> is that asset's size in METRES, recorded at 10 voxels/metre. These are the cross-scale pins: they are checked against a DIFFERENT kVoxelMeters than they were recorded at, which is the only thing that makes them non-circular (worldSize/skinScale*kVoxelMeters reduces algebraically to box/artVoxelsPerMetre and would agree with itself at any scale). Tolerance is 1.5 cells, since art is quantised and two scales may legitimately land on different whole cells. A move here means an asset changed physical size -- re-author or re-pin deliberately, do not rebaseline reflexively.
_scaleSash_about: 0.550 -> 0.300: the sash stopped wrapping the arms in d142be4 (wardrobe fit, 2026-09-04) and its pin was never updated; the scale gate failed against the base branch's own asset. Updated by hand alongside the grammar landing.
_wound_about: The wound model (src/test/selftest_wound.cpp). THRESHOLDS, not observations: these are read by the gates, so retuning what counts as a chip or how many blows take an arm costs a JSON edit and no rebuild. woundAccumMin/MaxHits is a BAND on purpose -- the property is that a blade is neither instant (the old three-threshold behaviour, which lands at 1) nor asymptotic (a model that only ever chips, which never severs at all), and an exact count would pin the suite to one rig's arm thickness and one set of gore.cut* values. woundChipMaxFraction is what would have caught the old radial carve: it removed a sphere the size of the limb. woundHeftHeavy is the second arm of the heft differential, and it must stay well clear of 1.0 or 'strictly fewer hits' becomes a coin flip on rounding.
_bodyStain_about: THRESHOLDS for the `body-stain` gate (DESIGN.md section 7, Blood on a body). bodyStainBoneMinFraction: of the bone voxels a deep kerf exposes, at least this fraction must carry a stain (bone is always shown bloodied to some degree; the soak floors it at gore.stainBoneMin). bodyStainWashMaxFraction: after 60 ticks in a box of water, the root limb may keep at most this fraction of the stained voxels it had after 30 ticks in a box of blood. bodyStainShallowMaxRise: standing 30 ticks in a two-voxel-deep pool, no limb voxel more than this many world voxels above the pool's top may carry a stain (the contact pass dilates a liquid cell by one voxel; blood on the thigh from an ankle-deep pool is the 2026-09-13 owner report).
_bodyCoat_about: THRESHOLDS for the `body-coat` gate (P1 of the body-coat scaffolding). A coat is a SUBSTANCE on a body voxel — a material id plus an amount — so these bound how it behaves as one. bodyCoatHoldMinFraction: over 150 ticks at the authored drying rate (blood: coat.decay 20 s per amount level, i.e. a 600-tick period) the cut limb must keep at least this fraction of the voxels its cut stained. bodyCoatDecayMaxFraction: with coat.decayScale set so that period becomes two ticks, the same count must fall to at most this fraction within the gate's 400-tick cap.
_ragdoll_about: THRESHOLDS for the `ragdoll` gate. A dummy knocked down by the X-detonate charge 6 voxels away must move its pelvis between min and max voxels in 1.5 s (min proves it flew, max proves it did not leave the county), and must be back on its feet within getUpMaxTicks.
_ragdoll_repeat_about: The fastest LIMB (m/s) of a wizard put through main.cpp's whole explosion block, standing and then again while already limp: ragdoll.maxLaunchSpeed (14) plus the fall it picks up. Before the rig skip list a limp hand took the per-body debris impulse (impulse / 0.3 kg) and the launch on top.
_ragdoll_burn_about: The player avatar on fire in stock cloth with the capsule proxy present: PlayerPushOut per tick (voxels) and total displacement over 400 ticks. Before the per-body-max + mass floor in PlayerPushOut: 62 vox in one tick, 432 vox before death.
_ragdoll_spin_about: The TUMBLE (ragdoll.blastLimbBias / blastSpinGain): the same charge at the ankles and then over the head, the same distance from the pelvis either way, must spin the rig in OPPOSITE directions about z by at least MinSpin rad/s and tip its pelvis's up axis by at least MinTiltGap between the two arms 12 ticks later. MaxLimbSpeedRatio holds the differential to a lean: no limb may leave the blast that many times faster than the slowest. Observed 2026-09-11 at bias 0.35 / gain 0.65: +0.61 and -0.54 rad/s, spread 1.12x / 1.18x, tilt gap 1.19.
_corpseArmor_about: THRESHOLDS for the `corpse-armor` gate (owner report 2026-09-13: an armoured NPC whose head had been cut off spasmed, flew apart while still jointed, and froze the game for minutes). The gate dresses the fixture in everything assets/items ships, cuts off the severable limb carrying the most armour, kills it, and watches the corpse for 3 s. MaxSpeedVox and MaxSpreadVox bound how fast and how far the remains travel. MaxPeggedTicks is the real claim: body-ticks spent at 90% of Jolt's own angular clamp. The PEAK spin is deliberately not bounded -- a limb thrown by a killing blow may touch 47.12 rad/s for a tick, and an assertion would have to sit above the clamp to pass at all -- but a limb that SITS there is being driven by its own constraints, which is the bug. Observed 2026-09-13 with the runaway net in: 69.1 vox/s, 34.5 vox, 1 pegged body-tick, net damped 0 / cut 0 / repaired 0, worst step 2.1 ms.
_ragdollDress_about: THRESHOLDS for the `ragdoll-dress` gate (owner report 2026-09-13: a clothed human going limp mid-fall 'becomes a crazy tangled mess ball of limbs and clothes that aren't actually connected properly'). A dressed human is made limp 200 voxels up and dropped under Jolt, then again on the spot at 30 m/s. ShellDrift/ShellTwist are how far a garment moves in the frame of the limb it is strapped to, and they are a CONSTANCY claim, not a smallness one: a worn shell is a kinematic follower with no constraint (MobLimb::wornHost), so its offset is derived and cannot change. LimbStretch is a joint's anchor measured in its PARENT's frame -- the point a ball joint welds -- so it catches a rig torn open by the anti-tunnel clamp without objecting to a limb that is merely rotating. Observed 2026-09-13: drift 0.000 / twist 0.06 deg / stretch 2.47 vox at 21.9 m/s. The SAME fixture with SANDVOX_NO_RIGWELD=1 (the A/B arm: jointed dynamic shells + the per-body clamp) gives drift 3.300, twist 151.50 deg and stretch 8.15 -- a greave rotated 151 degrees off the leg wearing it, which is the report in one number. The residual 2.4 vox of stretch is the solver's own softness at the landing impact and is the same in both arms of the new code.
_repose_about: repose gate (src/test/selftest_ca.cpp). THRESHOLDS, not observations: the runRiseMin/Max_* keys are read by the gate, so retuning what counts as a 2:1 or a 1:2 pile costs a JSON edit and no rebuild. run:rise is the pile's Manhattan reach over its peak height, so the ideal values are 3.0 / 2.0 / 1.0 / 0.5 for the four pure tiers -- the bands are wide because a 400-grain pile quantises hard (a peak of 4 vs 5 moves the ratio 25%) and because the apex starts as a 5x5 plateau rather than a point. The blend30/blend40 arms use REAL LOADER OUTPUT (PackRepose) and are the only arms that execute the per-grain blend hash at all; the gate asserts they differ from each other and sit between the pure tiers they mix, which is what catches a blend that has gone inert. The ORDERING is asserted separately and is the property that must not flap. awakeChunksMax is 0 on purpose: a lateral slide is the one powder move that does not lower a grain, so a nonzero count here means the termination argument in sim_step.wgsl's ANGLE OF REPOSE block is wrong, which is a rule-2 bug and not a threshold to raise. runRiseObserved_* are written by --rebaseline and read by nobody.
_cactus-fell_about: Added 2026-09-12 and PASSING since the same day. A saguaro-sized fixture (40 tall, one arm, on a sand bed) severed 8 cells up, in three arms: the game's own path (GPU support flag only, no forced mirror fetches), the brush's CPU door plus forced fetches, and a stone-pad control. The assertion that was red for a day is game-arm-body-falls: the severed top became a 1184-voxel body within three ticks and then stood in the air (fell 0.5 cells in 300 ticks) because ManageTerrain meshed the collider around it from a mirror copy that still held the top and only re-fetched a chunk while dirty and 8 ticks after the last request. The debris system now reads its own not-yet-mirrored writes through a per-chunk overlay (NoteGridWrite / pendingVacate_) in both the flood and the collider build; the game-arm body falls ~11 cells on its own. cactusFell.minDropCells is the floor on that fall.
_debris_about: KNOWN-FAILING since the tree overhaul (2026-08-29), and the cause is understood: the gate drops 54 rigid bodies into open forest at x 40-125 / z 420-490, and trees now have real branch structure, so bodies get CAUGHT IN CANOPIES instead of reaching the ground. Confirmed by voxel dump -- a 1,752-voxel body hung at y=221 with ground at y=199 and an autumn-birch canopy at y=231. Nothing about the tree code is wrong; the fixture assumed open ground. Two honest fixes are open: make foliage not support rigid bodies (physically right, a behaviour change in src/phys/debris.cpp), or move the drop zone somewhere trees do not grow (cheaper, but then nothing exercises debris landing in a forest).
_gas_about: THE WINDOW EDGE AS A SINK (docs/PLAN_gas_particles.md stage 1). THRESHOLDS, not observations -- the gates read every one of these, so retuning what counts as a sheet or how long a parcel gets to cross a face costs a JSON edit and no rebuild. gasLeaveSheetMax is the whole point of the change: before it, a gas voxel at the window's top face could not tell 'out of the world' from a solid wall and sheeted across the ENTIRE top chunk plane (up to 1,024 chunks) until it decayed. 8 is 'the plume's own footprint and nothing more'. There is NO pre-change control number for it on this tree and there cannot be one from a gate -- the old behaviour does not exist in this binary -- so the gate prints what it measured beside the bound rather than claiming a delta. gasLeaveProbeTick is where the two synchronous probes (the outer density box, the parcel page walk) are taken; it is a SEGMENT BOUNDARY in the run, not a read inside the tick loop. gasReenterMinLanded is 128 of 256 -- half, measured at 251 -- and not 256 on purpose: parcels die of their authored decay on the way across, so an exact count would re-pin this gate to reactions.json. gasReenterTicks is the WHOLE run and not just a deadline: the smoke a landing makes is a rising gas voxel like any other, and 60 ticks later it has climbed out of the census box and reached the window's own ceiling, where it correctly becomes a parcel again -- which read as '0 smoke voxels, 83 parcels alive' and had nothing to do with re-entry. Measure where the subject is.
_mobBurnKnown_about: KNOWN-FAILING SINCE 2026-09-04, and the cause is a change the owner asked for. Isolated solids now fall in the CA (soloSolid, sim_step.wgsl) -- and EMBER is a solid, so a lone ember drops and carries fire downward. The owner was asked directly whether hot materials should be excluded and chose to keep them falling. Two of this gate's subchecks measure that directly: 'heat across a joint' isolates cross-limb conduction by setting crossLimbPct to 0, and the thigh now takes 94/558 voxels at that setting against 0/558 before, because heat is arriving by falling onto it rather than through the joint; 'cloth vs flesh' wants cloth to burn faster than skin and now sees skin 96% consumed against 45%. ATTRIBUTED, not assumed: the same binary with the rule disabled passes both (thigh 0/558, skin 45%), measured at gate scope on both arms. This is the fire-down situation again -- a requested change makes a gate red and the honest record is the gate, not a compensating mechanic (the rejected `spark` material, 2026-09-03). Fixing it properly means the gate isolating cross-limb heat from AMBIENT heat, which is a real change to what it measures and belongs to the owner of the burn gates.

History: KNOWN-FAILING on the 011b642 line, NOT caused by the world-map P0 plumbing landed beside it on 2026-09-04 (that change binds an empty read-only buffer nothing reads; determinismHash is byte-identical to the pristine base, b9e443c7 both arms). _woundAccumulate_about: KNOWN-FAILING AT SUITE SCOPE ONLY, and NOT caused by the floaters/settle work landed beside it on 2026-09-03. The gate reports 'human/legU.L (1344 voxels): severed after 46 hits (band 2..14), byBlade=0, limb detached=0, +0 debris bodies' -- i.e. it hits the cap (woundAccumMaxHits*3+4) and the limb never detaches at all. Its neighbours pass on the SAME limb: wound-heft severs human/legU.L in 5 hits at heft 1.0 (inset 230) and wound-chip is green (inset 170), so this is specific to the inset-200 fixture site, not to melee or to the limb. THREE ARMS, all with a byte-identical detail line, rule out the obvious causes: (1) full 2026-09-03 debris changes + working-tree assets; (2) the same binary with SANDVOX_NO_SETTLE_SUPPORT=1, which restores pre-change settle behaviour and is HEAD-equivalent for this path (the P1 deferral counters all read 0 over the suite, so nothing else in that change alters behaviour); (3) the same binary against pristine HEAD assets via SANDVOX_ASSET_DIR, ruling out the concurrent materials.json/tuning.json edits in the working tree. And `--selftest --gate wound-accumulate` PASSES. So the cause is state an earlier gate leaves in the shared World -- CLAUDE.md rule 7 -- and it needs the owner of the wound gates, not a baseline edit, to actually fix. Recorded here so it stops masking real regressions; DO NOT treat this entry as the bug being understood.
_streamingKnown_about: KNOWN-FAILING AT SUITE SCOPE since at least 2026-09-04 on branch floaters-p0-p3, and NOT caused by the island/floater work landed beside it. Detail: 'ball chunk evicted=1, 0 glass voxels after re-entry' -- the glass ball streams out and comes back empty. ATTRIBUTED at the same scope on both arms: the full suite with the isolated-solid CA rule disabled (SANDVOX_ASSET_DIR pointing at a copy of the tree with soloSolid off) fails identically, and the ball is a solid radius-3 sphere resting on the ground that soloSolid cannot touch. _ai_about: Thresholds for the NPC AI gates (game/ai_behavior.h). Ranges are WORLD VOXELS centre-to-centre, times are 30 Hz sim TICKS. aiDummyMaxDriftVox/aiDummyMaxTurnRad are effectively zero on purpose: the `dummy` profile authorizes no drive and no turn at all, so anything above float noise is a code path that ignored the data rather than a tuning question. aiFaceToleranceRad is the facing error a static swordsman may settle at â€” it is a CONVERGENCE bound, checked after the turn has had aiFaceSettleTicks to finish, not a per-tick one. aiApproachOutOfBandTicks allows a few ticks outside the band over the whole hold window: a duelist that has just committed an attack deliberately gives ground, and the disengage step can graze the outer edge. The gate also records aiApproachArriveTick and aiFlatSpotRelief, which are MEASUREMENTS (how long the detour took, how flat the fixture's ground actually was) rather than bounds â€” a jump in either is what says 'the terrain moved' instead of 'the AI broke'.
_waterbody_about: Thresholds for the `waterbody` gate (docs/PLAN_water_master.md M1). The *TolPct and *Max keys are BOUNDS the gate fails against; the gate also records what it MEASURED through --rebaseline (waterbodyVolErrPct, waterbodyAreaErrPct, waterbodyBowlColumnErrPct, waterbodySurfaceSpread, waterbodyAwakeChunks). As of the M1 landing every measured error is EXACTLY 0.00% â€” the analytic container curve reproduces the authored lake's 2,782,656 eighths and 14,493 surface cells cell for cell, and the parabolic bowl's level-walk matches its column-walk at 128,214 cells on a real r54 tarn. The tolerance is 2% rather than 0 because the WORLD is not obliged to stay that way: pond life replaces water cells with kelp and reeds, and a ruin or a cave could intrude. A non-zero number here is not automatically a bug, but it IS a number that wants explaining before M2's ledger is built on the curve.
_waterbodyM3_about: M3 thresholds (components 6 + 7, the discharge law and the local excite). Pass H punches a 7x7 shaft through the authored lake floor into a sealed 29x29x18 chamber and lets the discharge law drain it for 90 ticks, then settles for 90 more. The identity is boxVoxelEighths + inFlightMpm - debit == boxVoxelEighths(0), and it is NOT a strict equality for either arm: the box contains a churning MPM pool with downstream physics the water-body system does not own (the CA thin-film handling of water sheeting down a shaft, the sun/water evaporation rule, the always-on wake trigger converting CA water beside the jet). Measured at the M3 landing: H1 (excite and splash off) -37 eighths against 35,381 drained and 40,342 in flight, 0.10%; H2 (shipped) -305 against 26,476 drained. `capped` is 0 in both, so the shave was never short and the ledger debited what it granted every tick — the residual is entirely downstream of the ledger. The bounds are assertions that the discharge is not a PUMP, not a claim that a churning pool is lossless.
_waterbodyShell_about: Plan section 9 item 2: the SHELL mitigation for component 7 was UNMEASURED in the design. At sim.drainExciteRadius 6 the shell converted 14,468 cells CUMULATIVELY over the 90-tick window (161/tick), against a solid ball at the r~25 a real vortex implies costing ~33,000 particles at once versus a ~40,000 largest-measured scene. The standing size is what sim.fluidExciteCeiling bounds (8,000); this is the flow through it. The 20,000 bound catches a radius change that reintroduces the ball.
_waterbodyDrainExcite_about: Plan section 9 item 1, REOPENED at M3. M2 measured the surface shave producing 0 excite candidates against 10.9 M cells inspected — the mechanism was not there, because the shave removes from the TOP. A real JET at a real throat is a different question, and the answer is that the mechanism IS there: 51,346 candidates over 90 draining ticks (570.5/tick) against 5,897,839 cells seen, which is the same order as WP5 own 169,616 over 400 ticks (424/tick) on worldlake. It is BOUNDED rather than absent — sim.fluidExciteCeiling and sim.fluidExciteRate are what hold it, and refusal is graceful because refused water is still settled water. The 3,000/tick bound is ~5x the measured value: it catches a regression into an unbounded burst without failing on the normal case.
_waterbodyRelevel_about: W1 thresholds (docs/PLAN_water_relevel.md, pass R). A 17x17x6 crater is bored into the authored lake's own floor and goes NOWHERE -- sealed stone on every side, sim.drainMaxEighthsPerTick 0 so the discharge cannot fire, and THE MPM SEAM OFF. That last one is pass H1's discipline reused: this is a rule that moves SETTLED water between columns, so the fixture must contain nothing else that moves settled water. Measured with the seam live and a 33x33x8 pit, the solver and the evaporation rule took 54,091 eighths out of the lake WITH THE RELEVEL DISARMED, left 64 chunks awake, and put an MPM block in a third of the surface chunks (which the measure correctly skips, so the mean came from 9,613 of 14,493 columns) -- every number the pass reported was a statement about the solver. Seam off, the same identity closes at EXACTLY +0 on both arms. TWO ARMS, rate 0 and the shipped rate, same worldgen, same ticks: without the control a spread inside budget cannot tell a working relevel from a crater the CA would have closed anyway, and the pass FAILS if the control also meets the budget -- a fixture that proves nothing is a fixture bug, not a pass. Measured at the W1 landing: CA alone 15 eighths, relevel 1, flat at 45 ticks, 12,855 given == 12,855 taken, credit 0, capped 0, 0 chunks awake. waterbodyRelevelSpread's UNIT IS EIGHTHS and the measure is the TOPMOST free surface per column -- whole voxels read flat while a forty-eighth cone still stands (the bug itself), and counting every free surface counts water sealed in a pocket under an air gap, which is not a lake surface and which wbSurface correctly never looks at. The crater size is arithmetic: a pit of half-width r and depth D spreads into a cone the CA stops flattening at 1 eighth per 2 cells, radius (48*D*r^2)^(1/3) and centre depth half that -- 14 eighths at 8 and 6, seven times the budget. The slack is 64 rather than 0 because a strict zero is a claim about rules this system does not own (evaporation, thin films); it measured exactly 0.
_waterbodyDiscover_about: W-D thresholds (docs/PLAN_water_relevel.md section 8, pass N). A pit is dug OUTSIDE the harness lake's disc with CellOps and filled with CellOps past sim.waterDiscoverMinEighths, and a body must APPEAR: a probe in the CPU registry, a GPU slot, WB_ADOPTED, and a measured volume near what was poured. The site is derived from the lake's own geometry (150 voxels west of its rim) rather than written as a literal, because the harness pool has moved once already. The fill stops one voxel BELOW the lowest rim in the footprint so the pool is contained on every column whatever the ground does -- a fixture that filled to the highest rim would be measuring a spill. Same discipline as pass R: no drain, no test tap, and THE MPM SEAM OFF, because this pass ends by measuring a rule that moves settled water and the fixture must contain nothing else that does. waterbodyDiscoverVolTolPct is wide (25) on purpose and is not a mass claim: the CA settles the pour, the top layer levels and the evaporation rule acts on a freshly exposed surface, so what this bounds is 'the body measured THIS pool' rather than half of it or the lake next door. The conservation identity belongs to passes A/H/R and is not restated here. waterbodyDiscoverCraterHalf/Depth are much smaller than pass R's 8/6 because the created pool is 33x33 rather than r68: the same crater would take a third of the pool's volume and the assertion would be about the drop, not the flatness. The NEGATIVE arm pours just under half the threshold into a real pit and requires the registry count unchanged AND no ledger slot live without a descriptor behind it -- the count alone would miss a probe raised and dropped inside the window. The ROUND TRIP saves the WTRB block, clears the registry, watches the descriptor go, reloads and requires re-adoption: nothing about the body's state is saved, so the GPU has to run Candidate -> Measuring -> Adopted again over the restored water, and a round trip that restored a LEDGER would pass in one tick and be the carried-descriptor bug.
_waterbodyDiscoverSpread_about: 3 and not pass R's 2 since 2026-09-14, and it is a MEASUREMENT and not a relaxation. The MPM leak fix (g2p's entry check) let pass H2 run to completion for the first time, which moved every later pass 383 ticks down the timeline -- the created body now adopts at tick 2091 instead of 1708, so its crater meets the M5 sweep schedule and the relevel dither at a different phase and settles one eighth wider. THE WINDOW WAS CHECKED FIRST and is not the cause: waterbodyDiscoverRelevelTicks is a fixed RunQuietTicks count that no timeline shift can truncate, and DOUBLING it to 240 measured the same 3 eighths. So 3 is where this pool converges, not where it had got to when the clock ran out. It stays a hard bound on a 33x33 pool -- a third of a voxel -- and it keeps its own key rather than sharing pass R's, so tightening R's 2 does not fail a pass about discovery.
_waterbodyWave_about: W2 thresholds (docs/PLAN_water_relevel.md section 4, pass S). Pass R's fixture EXACTLY -- same lake, same 17x17x6 crater, no drain, no test tap, the MPM seam off -- with sim.waveMode 1, so the only difference between the two passes is the pipe layer and every number here is comparable to one pass R already printed. Four assertions, four different bugs: the mass identity with the credit term (a pipe transfer lives in ONE word both ends read, so a non-zero number means the giver and the receiver disagreed about whether a pipe existed); Sigma|q| rises and then falls and stays fallen (momentum dissipated, never created); the body publishes flux-asleep inside waterbodyWaveSleepTicks (rule 2 -- a wave layer that cannot sleep has no idle-cost story); and the surface is flat at the end on pass R's own budget. THE DISSIPATION TEST IS BINNED and that is deliberate: Sigma|q| is an integer sum over ~14,000 dithered columns and a ring REFLECTS off the bank, focusing at the centre, which concentrates the same momentum into fewer columns and can lift the sum for a tick or two. A strict per-tick monotone assertion would be a knife edge measuring the bank's shape. waterbodyWaveBinTicks sets the bin, waterbodyWaveRiseTolPct is how much a bin may exceed its predecessor after the peak, and waterbodyWaveDecayFrac is how far below the peak the LAST bin must be -- the decay floor is what makes it a claim rather than a shrug. waterbodyWaveSpread has its own key rather than sharing pass R's for waterbodyDiscoverSpread's reason: two arms on one budget fail coupled.
_waterbodyW3_about: W3 thresholds (docs/PLAN_water_relevel.md section 5, pass T). The three sources that disturb a surface from OUTSIDE the heightfield: a blast, a swimmer and a live discharge. Every arm is a PAIR -- the knob at 0 and the knob on -- because either half alone proves nothing: an on-arm with no control cannot tell the feature from the CA, and an off-arm with no treatment cannot tell an identity from a knob that reaches no kernel. The two IMPULSE arms go through the game's own emitters (WaterBodyNoteBlast / WaterBodyNoteSwimmer, the same calls SubmitTick and main.cpp's frame loop make) and assert EXACTLY ZERO at knob 0: at 0 no record is queued, so TickParams::waterImpulseCount stays 0 and wbFlux's loop does not execute. Neither fires a real explosion -- detonating over the lake would carve voxels and the conservation line would be measuring sim_explode rather than the pipes. The SINK arm is a DIFFERENTIAL and not an identity, because the fixture itself (pass H's shaft and sealed chamber, cell for cell) disturbs the surface whether or not the sink is on; what it asserts is that Sigma|q| over the drain window is strictly greater with the knob on, and it FAILS rather than skips when the shaft never discharged, because a sink generated from WBS_EMIT cannot be measured in a fixture with no emission. waterbodyW3SwimKnob and waterbodyW3SinkKnob are the gate's own knob values, deliberately larger than the shipped defaults so the arm is measured clear of the noise floor.
_envTruth_about: Thresholds and records for the `env-truth` gate (docs/PLAN_environment_truth.md P-H): one synthetic one-biome world per biome file, the real GPU worldgen, measured against the biome page's prediction. Trees are asserted per LATTICE SITE against an expected interval [lo, hi] (nearWater rows sit in hi only), widened by envTruthSigmas binomial sigmas and envTruthTreeSlack whole trees. Cover rows are asserted only where nothing but the row can place the material (no ground-flora chain, no proc cactus): tolerance is the largest of sigmas x binomial sigma, envTruthCoverRelTol x expected, and envTruthCoverAbsTolPct of the columns (the patch mask is modelled in distribution, and its realised fraction over ~256 cells wanders a few percent). envTruthSkinMinPct / envTruthSubsoilMinPct bound the ground skin at y == h and the subsoil at y == h - skinDepth. The envTruthTreesPerHa_* and envTruthUnauthoredPct_* keys are RECORDS written by --rebaseline, not bounds: the second is the share of columns wearing a plant no cover row placed (the shader's hard-coded undergrowth/flower chain), the number that should go to zero when that chain becomes authored rows.
_caSlopeHybrid_about: ca-slope-hybrid is the ONE gate here left red on purpose, because what it reports is a behaviour and not a stale expectation. Same script as `ca-slope` but at the SHIPPED sim.fluidExciteMode 1, so the CA and the MPM solver both move the water. Measured 2026-08-29: 768 eighths poured down a stepped ramp, 79.4% reach the catch basin against the 90% the CA-only arm clears. Everything else about the run is clean -- mass is EXACT to the eighth, the ledger never parts company, all 12 structure chunks are asleep from tick 100. What is missing is 24 eighths perched on the deck as voxels and 134 eighths carried by 134 live MPM particles that are not in the basin. Those particles are PERMANENT, not slow: the live count by quarter of the run is 134/134/134/134, dead-flat, and over the whole run 1342 excited -> 1342 emitted with 1208 settled and 1208 dead, so settling is the only way a particle dies and these 134 have stopped settling. The mechanism is WP3's settle veto refusing to convert perched water (correctly -- it would create a floating puddle) combined with nothing moving it downhill, so the water parks on the slope in particle form. That is the gate's founding complaint ("on a hill it'll clump and settle on the hill instead of flowing down") coming back in a different representation, plus a per-tick solver cost that never goes away, which is rule 2. Do not rebaseline this to 79.4%: the number is the report, not the bug.
_perf_about: Budgets for the advisory `perf` gate, moved out of C++ literals (they were 8.0 and 16.0 in selftest_sim.cpp) so retuning them costs a JSON edit rather than a rebuild — CLAUDE.md's own rule, which this gate was the last one violating. They were written at a smaller kVoxelMeters and have been unreachable since it changed, so the gate sat red in this file for months asserting an aspiration instead of detecting a regression; a permanently-red advisory gate trains everyone to skip the line. Measured on the reference machine (RTX 3060 Ti, 2026-08-29): sim 10.11 ms/tick on the deliberately-active benchmark scene (explosions and particles every tick, against a 33 ms tick budget at 30 Hz) and 21.37 ms/frame for the best of the four 1080p render passes. The bounds below are those numbers with ~30% headroom, which is a regression detector: a change that makes the sim or the raymarch a third slower fails here. They are NOT a target — if the numbers get better, tighten them.
_fluidReact_about: The `fluid-react` gate used to assert `standing + live + consumed == placed` exactly, and it came up 37 of 2704 eighths short (1.4%) every run, deterministically. That is not a leak: FA_CONSUMED counts eighths eaten off EXCITED fluid, but the authored rule {self: plant, neighbor: water, neighborBecomes: plant} also runs in the CA on SETTLED water voxels, and nothing counts those. The missing water is standing in the world as the new plant cells the gate itself counts and calls a pass. The gate now asserts the properties that survive that: no water is created, the gap never exceeds 8 eighths per plant that grew, and the gap stays under this fraction. 3% against 1.37% measured is ~2x headroom — enough that a plant bed of a different size does not fail it, tight enough that water vanishing with nothing to show for it still does.
_bodies_about: debris and settle-back were carried as KNOWN-FAILING from the terrain scale pass with a documented cause -- BuildTerrainPatches waking every body within 24 voxels faster than SettleBodies' 60-consecutive-inactive-tick countdown. THAT CAUSE WAS WRONG, and finding out cost one run once the reporter recorded the wake at the point it happens instead of leaving a bare count (CLAUDE.md rule 6). Measured 2026-08-29: some body managed a 208-tick quiet run against the 60 a settle needs, and the last terrain wake landed 120 ticks before the end. The wake path is innocent. The two gates had two unrelated causes and neither was shared. settle-back: the 3x3x3 block was dropped onto raw procedural terrain at (80,80), which the terrain overhaul turned into a slope; it rolled 13 voxels downhill and came to rest at an angle more than 20 deg off axis, where SettleBodies deliberately refuses to resample it (PLAN B6, `kAlignCos`). Body high water was 1, so nothing else ever existed -- the block simply never qualified, and the refusal was correct. The gate now builds its own flat pad, because the shape of worldgen at one hardcoded (x,z) was never its subject. debris: ONE 21-voxel piece of ejecta, thrown clear of the 3x3x3 CPU mirror by the 500-strength blast, ended at (52.8,111.0,212.4) -- 110 voxels under the ground at y=221. ManageTerrain can only build collision for a chunk the cache already holds, PostStep only despawns bodies that leave the 512-voxel residency window, and between those two boundaries a body is simulated with no ground under it: it tunnels into the rock and then never sleeps because the solver keeps depenetrating it. That IS a real defect, it is a physics/streaming design call rather than a test fix, and it is now bounded by debris.buriedMax below instead of hiding inside a red gate. The gate itself asserts the thing it was written for -- every body still ABOVE ground settles -- and goes red if the buried count grows.
_debris_buried_about: How many debris bodies may end a `debris` run buried below local terrain. 1 is what the gate's blast currently produces (see _bodies_about). This is a KNOWN DEFECT held under a bound, not a tolerance anyone wants: the right value is 0, and it gets there when a body whose surrounding chunks are not cached yet stops being integrated against terrain that does not exist. Raising this number is not a fix.
_mobBurn_about: Floor on how much of the player's FLESH a 90-tick immersion in fire must drive past the sear (flesh_charred + flesh_cinder as a percentage of all flesh). The subtest it guards used to count flesh_cooked as 'charred', so a body that only seared scored the same as one that burned -- which is how 'the player only blackens along the outlines of its limbs' sat under a green gate. Measured 9.8% before the world-pitch neighbour reading in MobSystem::BurnOneLimb and 23.7% after; the floor sits between them.
_fireDown_about: Floor, as a percentage of a 9x9 layer, on how much of each measured leaf layer the `fire-down` gate must consume. The gate asks the one question nothing else in the suite asks: can fire travel DOWNWARD at all. Before the leaf_burning stage and the dir:down emit siblings landed the answer was structurally no -- `fire` is a gas that rises with probability 1 in calm air and every emit rule in reactions.json was dir:up, so the only downward heat path in the world was a stationary tag:hot solid touching the voxel below it, which foliage did not have. Both arms of the gate scored ~0% at HEAD before that change and the fixture is deliberately sized so they saturate after it, which is why one floor serves all four layers rather than four tuned numbers. If a burning tree ever feels wrong the lever is leaf_burning's decay TOTAL in reactions.json (80 per-mille = ~12.5 ticks of exposure per leaf), not this floor.
_weakFlame_about: The ratio the `weak-flame` gate asserts between a fuel's ignition chance from a STATIONARY hot neighbour (ember, lava, burning tissue) and from `fire`, the drifting flame gas. It is the reciprocal of the `neighborChance.fire` multiplier authored on every ignition rule in reactions.json (0.125 = 8), checked against the COMPILED table so a typo in the field, a refused expansion or a synthetic tag that leaked onto fire fails loudly instead of silently restoring the old spread rate under a moved hash. Change the multiplier in reactions.json and this number together. HALVED AGAIN TO A SIXTEENTH on owner request 2026-09-03 ("make the chance the fire voxels, the ones that move through the air, have 50% even less chance to catch things on fire"), in the same change that let a burning limb heat the limb next to it. Those two go together: the drifting flame was the ONLY path from a burning torso to the legs, which is why it could not be weakened before without putting out the one route body fire had, and Mob::BuildCrossLimbHeat is what replaced it. Authored as "neighborChance": { "fire": 0.0625 } on every ignition rule in reactions.json; this number is its reciprocal and the two move together or this gate fails, which is the point of it.
_floaters_about: Thresholds for the `floaters` gate, which asserts the one thing the rest of the suite cannot see: what the grid <-> rigidbody handoff LEFT BEHIND. A CLASS_SOLID voxel never moves in the CA, so island detection is the only mechanism that makes solid matter fall and anything it declines to convert hangs there forever. `maxComponents` is how many unsupported solid components the bounded sweep may find in the fixture box -- 0, because the gate builds the box itself and nothing in it has any business floating. `minVoxels` is the size floor below which a component is not worth reporting: single stray voxels are ejecta the particle system is still carrying, not structures. Both are bounds the gate fails against; the *Observed keys are what the last run measured and are written by --rebaseline. The gate's detail line also prints DebrisSystem::FloaterProbe cumulatively for the whole run -- read `deferred*` as the repairs working (matter held in the grid on purpose and re-queued) and `deferGaveUp` / `solidRubbleInPlace` / `stuckEventDropped` as matter that actually got away.
_treeFell_about: Thresholds for the `tree-fell` gate, which asks the `floaters` question of the thing the owner actually reports: burn a tree down and lone voxels and 2..8-voxel clumps hang in the air, cut one through the trunk and it keeps standing. RECORDED KNOWN-FAILING ON PURPOSE for the CUT half only, which is the SPEC for work not yet built: a tree is 88-217 voxels tall and up to 230 across against kMaxRegionCells 80, kMaxIslandVoxels 32000 and DebrisVoxel's int8 body-local coords, so `cut-trunk-fells-the-tree` cannot pass until large islands can be sharded into jointed sub-bodies -- docs/PLAN_rigidbody_islands.md. THE BURN HALF PASSES AT ZERO and is a live regression detector: `maxSingles` and `maxClumps` are 0. The gate burns the tree, samples the NATURAL burn-out every 100 ticks for 1500 ticks (floating components beside cells still hot -- residue that stays up while the hot count falls is the machinery, residue that tracks it is the fire), then QUENCHES grid and bodies so time-to-clean measures the handoff alone. Measured: natural series 15,16,5,3,4 floating with 890->215 hot; quenched 0/0/0 at +400, clean within 100 ticks. What got it there: isolated solids fall in the CA (soloSolid; powder counts only below), a solid that turns to powder in place stops holding things up (flagSupportLoss), the event queue no longer head-of-line blocks or drops, the cooldown re-arms, scans are budgeted by cells visited with the flood seeded from the changed box, settle-back refuses over an unfetched chunk and re-judges its stamp, and the sweep counts floating on a denser liquid as support. `felledFraction` and `maxStandingVoxels` are the cut half. The *Observed keys are written by --rebaseline. AT SUITE SCOPE the burn half currently shows ONE >=8 clump: the whole 16,171-voxel crown, hanging after the trunk burned through under it. That is the large-island cap (a 53-wide crown never fits a 64^3 scan box, so it is anchored at the boundary every time), i.e. the cut-half limitation appearing in the burn half, not a small-clump regression; the gate-scope run of the same tree reads 0/0/0. It passes with the sharded-island work and not before.
_terrain_about: Thresholds and measurements for the `terrain` gate. The *Max/*Slack/*Margin keys are BOUNDS the gate fails against and are hand-tuned; the *Observed keys are what the last run measured and are written by --rebaseline. Retuning a bound is a JSON edit, not a rebuild.
_swingPlaneStatus_about: swing-plane PASSES as of the combat phase C+D merge (2026-08-31, branch combat-final). THREE prior reports quoted three different sets of numbers for this gate because each measured a different tree; this key states what the MERGED tree measures and how it got there. PHASE C repaired the fixture, three faults, none of them the residency window the pre-C text blamed. (1) THE TARGET WALKED: the dummy is a 'human', human.json declares no 'behavior', so MobSystem::DecideIntent fell through to the legacy wander and a human walks 31.5 vox/s -- spawned at z 261, read at z 269.4 eight ticks later, and the sweep swept where it used to be. Fixed as DATA: the fixture asks for the 'dummy' behaviour profile by name. (2) THE ANCHOR MIXED UNITS: World::WindowOrigin() is in CHUNKS and the gate added kWorldN/2 VOXELS to it -- a no-op at the origin, which is why it read as a suite-only failure, and 44 voxels outside the window once 'streaming' had shifted it. (3) THE READY DROVE INTO THE AZIMUTH STOP: the open-loop ready pushed rightward from a hanging arm; it is closed-loop on the stroke state now. Underneath all three sat a REAL bug only the repaired fixture could see: Mob::ApplyWeaponArm carried its own copy of the hinge-angle projection and did not wrap it into (-pi, pi] the way ClampHinge does, so a forearm in the far quaternion hemisphere read as +4.89 rad there and -1.39 rad here, and the elbow clamp threw 1.39 rad of a good solve away on every committed horizontal cut. Both now call anim.h AnimHingeAngleAbout. PHASE D re-authored the grip: assets/items/{sword,cleaver}.json rotate [0,0,-90] instead of [0,-90,0], which puts a neutral blade down the arm's own line instead of across it, and dropped melee.wristMaxAngle 2.80 -> 1.50 on the strength of an A/B run against the OLD fixture. THE MERGE FOUND ONE INTERACTION, and it was that wrist cap. The blade asks the wrist for a FULL orientation delta -- direction AND ROLL -- and the neutral grip stands about pi of roll away from what a committed cut wants, so what STEERING gets is the cap minus that standing tax. Old grip at 2.80 left ~1.2 rad free, which is what phase C measured against; new grip at 1.50 left ~0.0 and the arm line reported 'wrist 1.50/3.00' -- pegged -- in every single pass. The cap is 3.10 now, leaving ~1.1 rad free, i.e. the same steering budget phase C had. MEASURED ON THE MERGED TREE, cap 1.50 -> 3.10: follow residual 3.66 -> 0.34 vox (bound 4.30); A commanded->posed residual 8.65 -> 5.51, posed az sweep 2.96 -> 2.23 against a commanded 2.38; B az drift 2.28 -> 0.09, out-of-plane 0.88 -> 0.19, residual 7.31 -> 0.26; C ratio 4.39 -> 2.21, travel agreement 0.952 -> 1.000, residual 6.84 -> 0.25. Five failing checks became zero. THE GATE ALSO HAD A MEASUREMENT BUG, found the same way and fixed here: pass D summed RAW atan2 deltas, so one crossing of the +-pi branch behind the shoulder turned +2.25 rad of rightward travel into -4.03 and reported 'steady rightward mouse carries the tip LEFT'. Azimuth is unwrapped before it is ranged now, in pass D and in runStroke's az min/max and backstep counters, and the wrap count is printed. Same bug, third instance on this branch, after ApplyWeaponArm's hinge and npc-styles' arc accumulator. STILL OPEN, and it is content rather than code: the standing ~pi of wrist roll is a GRIP question. Authoring the neutral roll into the item JSONs would let wristMaxAngle come back down to a real wrist; the naive attempt ([180,0,-90]) makes the follow residual worse (8.08), so it is a piece of work, not a sign flip. Also still true: human.json bounds the right upper arm to 30 degrees past the midline, so the last third of a committed horizontal cut sits on that stop -- which is why planarity is stated on the COMMANDED arc and the rig's deviation is bounded separately via rigResidualFrac, with a printed attribution line naming which joint limit spent it.
_swingPlane_about: swing-plane thresholds. The gate measures the SWORD'S world trajectory about the live shoulder joint, through the whole IK/clamp/physics pipeline, so every bound here is in radians of tip arc or in fractions of the tip's own radius -- never in voxels, which would move with kVoxelMeters. Retune by editing this file; nothing here costs a rebuild, and as of the phase C/D merge the gate also calls ApplyMeleeTuning, so melee.* in tuning.json reaches it too (before that it ran on the compiled melee.h initialisers, and a JSON edit moved every OTHER melee gate while leaving this one byte-identical -- which reads as 'the wrist is not the constraint' and really means 'the knob is not connected'). azSweepMin/elSweepMin are how much arc a committed flick must actually produce; elDevMax/azDevMax are how much of the OTHER angle it may leak into; planarMaxFrac bounds how far the sweep may wander out of the plane its own first and last radii span; frontMinFrac is the most-backward the tip may get, as a fraction of its radius (negative = a little behind the shoulder is tolerated, the arm does swing past); diagRatioMax keeps a diagonal diagonal; hitFarFrac is how much further the far limb must be than the near one for the wound-placement pair to mean anything; edgeGainMin is how much better an edge-on cut must rate than a flat-on one. rigResidualFrac is how far the POSED sword may sit from the COMMANDED tip as a fraction of the commanded radius -- that gap is human.json's authored joint limits, NOT a swing property, so it is loose on purpose and is paired with the arm-diagnostic line that names the limit; sweepTrackMax is the strict one, radians of commanded ARC the physical sword is allowed to lose. steerBackMax was a literal in selftest_swing.cpp until the merge and is here now for the usual reason (a bound in source costs a rebuild to tune). It is how many of pass D's 22 equal mouse steps may send the tip backwards; the merged tree measures 4 with the atan2 unwrap in place, and the bound is 4. That is TIGHT ON PURPOSE -- it is the one check that says the blade can be aimed at all -- but it is also the number to look at first if pass D ever flakes, because 4 of 22 has no headroom left.
_swingPlaneFollow_about: followMaxFrac 0.35 -> 0.45 (2026-09-01). NOT a loosening to make a change pass: the gate now PRINTS what spends it. Pass 0 drives +-12 px/tick from the take-over seed, and restoring the sword grip to [0,-90,0] moved that seed (the tip is a blade-length forward of the fist instead of a blade-length down the arm, r 12.29 -> 11.20), so the leftward half of the same drive now reaches the RIGHT SHOULDER's authored reach stop -- `reach: normal [1,0,0] max 30` on human.json. The new `swing-plane 0 (at worst)` line attributes it: tick 23, steer 1.00, wrist 2.54/2.54 (not clipped), ikMiss 0.00, shoulder clamp 0.46 rad, and 0.46 rad at the shoulder is 4.40 voxels at the point. That is the same CAN-THIS-BODY-MAKE-IT quantity `swingPlane.rigResidualFrac` (0.85) admits for passes A-C, and the gate header note says so in as many words. Tightening it is a RIG change, not a threshold edit.
_swingPlaneRest_about: R/G/H thresholds -- the passes that measure a sword NOBODY IS SWINGING. Added 2026-09-01 for four owner-reported regressions the whole dynamic set was green through: a hilt buried in the fist at rest, a wrist that only aligned mid-swing, a guard pointing the blade straight down, an arm driveable behind the body with an elbow that bent either way. R reads the AUTHORED GRIP (at Idle nothing steers, so the item renders at handQ*gripRot), G reads the guard hold after the wrist steer ramp has settled, H drives into the azimuth stop and the elbow's authored hinge. Angles are degrees so nothing here moves with kVoxelMeters; the elbow fold is a dot product (-1 straight, +1 folded) so a straight-arm solve cannot read as hyperextension.
_swingPlaneArmBehind_about: armBehindMinFrac -0.45 -> -0.62 (2026-09-01, the chirality fix). The bound is on the POSED TIP, and -0.45 was sized on the mirrored solve, where the weapon-side stop drove the arm ACROSS the model and its tighter authored range held the blade nearer the front. On the true weapon side the deep-stop wind-up legitimately cocks the blade further behind the shoulder line (measured -0.55 of r, tip -6.12 vox at r 11.20, hand -2.00). The ARM is what the report was about, and the arm is bounded separately now: melee.handBackFrac pins the driver hand at 0.05 of reach behind the frontal plane, and pass H prints the posed hand beside the tip.
_combat_about: NPC combat gates (src/test/selftest_combat.cpp). npc-strike/npc-block/npc-styles/duel, plus the two feel gates combat-tuning/combat-cues at the front of kOrder. gapVox is how far apart the fixtures stand, WORLD VOXELS -- an arm is 0.6 m and the sword 0.55 m, so a target much past 12 voxels is out of reach and the gate would be asserting that a sword cannot reach two metres. windupTicksMin is the TELEGRAPH: a swing that resolves faster than this is unreadable and unavoidable, which is the failure mode having no UI indicator has to be defended against. lostVoxMin is how much flesh one cut must remove. guardAz/guardEl/guardReachFrac aim the blocking defender's point; the gate then aims the ATTACKER at the midpoint of the blade it reads back, so the parry is geometric rather than hoped for. guardReachFrac went 0.75 -> 0.95 at the phase C/D merge and the reason is timing, not aim: with the re-authored grip the blade lies ALONG the arm, so a guard held close keeps the edge behind the plane where the attacker's blade first reaches flesh, and the parry fired only AFTER 329 voxels had already been opened. Held further out it intercepts on the way in -- measured, defender flesh 3328 -> 3328, 0 bodies hit, blade hp 30.0 -> 27.5. melee.blockGapM went 0.14 -> 0.22 m for the same geometric reason (the two swept edges now pass within 2.44 voxels where the old grip gave 0.86). dominanceMin decides when an authored style COUNTS as azimuth- or elevation-dominant (below it, the style is read as a diagonal and both channels are required); minSweepRad and minThrustVox are the floors for a channel actually having travelled -- radians for the two angular ones, VOXELS for the thrust's radius, which is why they are two keys and not one. diagRatioMax and thrustSwingMax were literals in the .cpp and are keys here now (a bound in source costs a rebuild to tune), but they are at their ORIGINAL values on purpose -- see npc-styles below. duel.ticks is how long two duelists are left alone; duel.lostVoxMin is deliberately 1, because the claim is BOTH sides bled and not how much -- which one wins is a single RNG draw and asserting on it is how a gate becomes a flake. duel.awakeChunksMax is CLAUDE.md rule 2 on a fight: gore and blood are CellOps into the grid and must not wake the world. npcStrike.lostVoxMin WAS 20 and is 3 since 2026-09-14, because the 20 was never measuring the depth of a cut -- it was measuring DISMEMBERMENT. Under the old gore.woundImpactSeverScale (8) a swing's tip ran 390-400 vox/s against limb bars of 72-160, so every strike tripped the instant impact sever, a limb left the body, and FleshVoxels dropped by hundreds; the gate's own fixture comment ('the first landed strike took this dummy from 3092 flesh voxels to ZERO') is that world. With the scale at 0 the structural model finally runs, and one real swing at 400 vox/s legitimately takes a SHALLOW bite: measured 8 / 4 / 1 voxels on three strikes, because the blade crosses 13 world voxels per tick and the kerf is placed once per body per tick rather than smeared along that travel. Raising the kerf to reach 20 was tried and rejected -- at depth 0.2+0.5p / length 1.4 the best strike reached 16 but wound-heft's heavy arm severed in 2 hits, i.e. it bought the number back by re-approaching the one-blow dismemberment this whole change removes. 3 keeps the claim that catches the real regression (all three strikes are 1-voxel clips) with margin against the observed best of 8; 'cuts add up' is wound-accumulate's claim, not this gate's. If a smeared kerf ever lands (scale cut.length by the blade's travel through the body), re-measure and raise this.
_npcBlockStatus_about: npc-block and npc-styles flipped fail -> pass 2026-09-01, by the combat-regression fixes rather than by a threshold edit: restoring the sword grip to [0,-90,0] and bounding the elbow bend plane changed where a guarding blade sits and how a styled stroke reaches. Both were verified in a FULL --selftest (rule 7: a gate subset is not a small selftest) on the same tree, determinismHash f7ca2a1c unmoved, 0 page faults. WATCH THE MARGIN ON npc-block: the two swept edges closed to 2.18 voxels against a melee.blockGapM of 0.22 m = 2.20 voxels, i.e. 1%. That gap was RAISED from 0.14 m at the phase C/D merge specifically because the along-the-arm grip left a defender's edge further from its own fist; the grip is back and the measured closing distance came back with it, so 0.22 is now sized for the geometry that ships rather than for the one it was tuned against. If this gate starts flapping, that knob is the first place to look.
_npcBlock_about: npc-block is KNOWN-FAILING IN THE FULL SUITE ONLY, and unlike npc-styles beside it the MECHANISM is fine -- what fails is the fixture's margin. At `--selftest --gate npc-block` the merged tree reports: 1 block event, stroke arrested, defender flesh 3328 -> 3328 (not one voxel lost), 0 bodies hit, blocking blade hp 30.0 -> 27.5, the two swept edges passing within 2.44 voxels. That is the whole feature working. In the full suite the same fixture measures 3.23 voxels between the edges, which is outside melee.blockGapM (0.22 m = 2.2 voxels, plus the attacking blade's own ~0.75 of half-width), so no parry fires and the cut goes through. THE CAUSE IS SCOPE, exactly as CLAUDE.md ordering rule 7 warns: a --gate subset is not a small --selftest. `streaming` shifts the residency window ~20 chunks before this gate runs in the suite, so the two fighters stand on different ground -- window chunks (0,0,0) alone against (20,-2,-7) in the suite -- and the guard pose settles a little differently on it. 2.44 and 3.23 are the same fixture on two hillsides. WHY IT ONLY MATTERS NOW: phase D's re-authored grip lays the blade ALONG the arm, so the defender's edge sits further from its own fist and the same guard leaves more slack; the old grip closed to 0.86 voxels and had margin to spare at any scope. Two knobs were already moved for this and both were measured, not guessed -- melee.blockGapM 0.14 -> 0.22 m and npcBlock.guardReachFrac 0.75 -> 0.95 (hold the point further out and it intercepts on the way IN, which is what took the flesh loss from 329 voxels to zero). WHAT NOT TO DO: push blockGapM to 0.25+ so the suite number fits. It would work, and it would be tuning the GAME to one hillside -- the tuner's own warning line is 0.3 m, past which a defender parries blows that passed a foot from its blade and the AI reads as invincible. WHAT TO DO: make the fixture scope-independent, the way `voxregion` and phase C's own window-anchor fix did -- pin the window for the gate, or stand the pair on a built pad rather than on whatever terrain the previous gate left under them (`settle-back` was repaired in exactly this way and for exactly this reason, see _bodies_about). Then this entry goes away and the bound goes back to being about blades.
_npcStyles_about: The thrust check was RESTATED ON THE COMMANDED ARCS 2026-09-01, which is fix (3) this note used to prescribe: an absolute cap on the POSED arc was the one claim in the gate not stated on the commanded stroke, it sat 1% under its bound in the full suite, and the discrete-strikes torso lean (melee.torsoShare) finally pushed it over -- the lean moves the very shoulder the posed arc is measured about, so posed az went 2.19 -> 2.72 on a commanded 0.36. The threshold was NOT raised (the note's own rule: a bound moved to cover a named fault never moves back); the CLAIM moved to the coordinate every other dominance check already uses, and it is scope-stable there (the old --gate-vs-suite flapping was this same posed cap measured on two hillsides). thrustSwingMax 1.0 now bounds the commanded arcs. The posed sword keeps its own claim: it has to have MOVED in the authored channel.
_playerStyles_about: player-styles (src/test/selftest_swing.cpp): every authored style replayed through the PLAYER'S discrete path (StepStrokeProgram + MeleeState, camera basis, aim (0,0)) on the real avatar rig, npc-styles' per-style claims restated there plus two of its own: the driver must COMMIT Slash when a style's authored cut speed demands it (edge alignment rides on the commit; a thrust is exempt by its own arithmetic -- its cut rides the radial channel, which commitSpeed never sees, and the damage sweep keys on the CURSOR for exactly that reason), and the blade must stay clear of the wielder's own head -- measured INDEPENDENTLY of the keep-out clamp's inputs (physics WeaponEdge segment vs the head limb's joint), every tick the arm is claimed, windup included. headClearMin is the BOUND; headClearObserved is what the suite last measured (2.12 vox at seeding, styles ranging 2.1-3.7). LIVE tuning on purpose, unlike swing-plane's pinned knobs: the subject is the shipped strike.
_smoke_about: Pinned hash sequences for --vk-smoke and --vk-smoke-loud. Each entry is [tick, hash]. tick 0 = worldgen. Re-record with --rebaseline.
_openness_about: The openness (sky-visibility) grid, docs/PLAN_gi.md 2. Both are FRACTIONS of full sky visibility, read straight out of the byte the pass wrote. roofedMax is the +Y face of a BUILT 45x45 stone floor (floating 4.8 m over the real surface, found by scanning the voxel column) under a 45x45 stone roof 1.4 m up; openMin is the +Y face of the roof's own top. Since 2026-09-05 the fixture owns both slabs, so no landform can put the probe cell in a pit its 4x4 block cannot march from (that was the known failure after the harness pads went). Ranges, never equality: the five ray directions are fixed and the value is quantised to a byte.
_giBounce_about: One-bounce indirect light, docs/PLAN_gi.md 3. A white bone wall stands on the -X edge of a floating 41x41 leaves slab at noon; the gate renders the wall's +X face with render.giStrength at its default and again at 0 and takes the mean per-channel difference over the middle of the frame, in 0..255 units. minGreenDelta is the least green the bounce must add; minGreenOverRed is how much more green than red it must add (a grey brightening is not a bounce off green).
_bodyShade_about: Rigidbodies are rasterized cubes (debris.wgsl vsBody/fsBody, shaded by litColorS in common.wgsl), not raymarched, and until 2026-09-04 that path had NO sun-shadow term: a body received 100% of the key light wherever it stood (measured ~3.2x too bright in an ordinary cast shadow, ~10.4x indoors). The gate stands a 5^3 stone rigidbody on a 45x45 deck under a 45x45 roof at noon and renders three arms of ONE world state: body draw count 0 (which yields the body pixel mask by difference), body with shadows off, body with shadows on. It compares how much each surface DIMS when shadows go on, as a fraction of its own lit level -- a ratio, so a dark body and a pale deck are comparable. Measured at the landing: body 0.532, deck 0.562, ratio 0.95. With the body path shadow forced off the body dims 0.000 (bit-identical frames) and the ratio is 0.00, which is the regression this exists to catch. minRatio/maxRatio are a deliberately wide band: a body legitimately gets no voxel AO and no GI bounce and its faces are not axis-aligned with the grid, so it is not expected to track the deck exactly. minTerrainResponse guards the FIXTURE -- if the deck itself is not in shadow the ratio denominator is noise and the gate reports that instead of blaming the body path.
_giNightfall_about: No block-face keeps yesterday's sun, docs/PLAN_gi.md 3. Two floating 4x4 plates are charged by the openness walk at noon and then carved down to a single column each -- one on a column openSunSample probes, one on a block corner it does not -- and walked 24 more ticks at midnight. maxRemainPct is the most of the noon luminance either word may still hold; minDayLum is the floor the charge itself must clear, so "it faded" cannot pass on a word that was never lit. Before the five-column probe and the unconditional fade both words held 100%.
_caveTime_about: A sealed room does not know what time it is (selftest_render.cpp GateCaveTime). A 24-voxel stone box with 2-voxel walls is stamped well above the ground, the camera is put inside it aiming into a corner, and the same view is rendered at the sun's highest and lowest tick; the numbers are the mean LINEAR luminance of the middle of the frame (the bytes are gamma-encoded and these values sit where the encode exaggerates small differences). maxDayNightRatio is the most the noon frame may exceed the midnight one -- before 2026-09-11 the reader multiplied the day/night hemisphere ambient by render.opennessFloor, so a sealed cave was lit at a flat 30%% of the time of day and the --shot stone room swung 8.6x. minDayLum stops "unchanged" being satisfied by rendering black; maxFracOfMeadow stops it being satisfied by dimming the whole world, by requiring the box to stay far darker than the open ground it is buried beside.
_glow_about: The glow field, src/sim/world.h kGlowBytes and assets/shaders/sim_glow.wgsl: a coarse world-space field of emitter light that the raster body and mob paths can read with ONE buffer load, because giGather needs nine rays plus voxels/pageTable in the fragment stage and they have neither. Four passes over one fixture -- a 4x4x4 block of crystal (a solid mineral with emission 120, no reactions, buried 12 cells under the surface so nothing can move it and the floating-voxel pass cannot lift it into a rigid body). A: the source word counted all 64 emitting cells and is bright. B: the field one 4-cell block away, ACROSS a chunk boundary, is nonzero. C: the field two CHUNKS away -- outside the producer 3x3x3 gather stencil by construction -- is zero, which is what stops a producer that returned bright everywhere from passing A, B and D. D: the emitter is replaced with stone and both go back to EXACTLY zero. maxFarLum and maxRemainPct are 0 and not a small tolerance on purpose: unlike the irradiance grid this field is a pure recompute with no memory, so anything above zero is a bug rather than a decay that has not finished. minSrcLum/minNearLum are the floors that stop the zero assertions passing on a field that was never lit.
_denoise_about: The shading-LOD filter, assets/shaders/denoise.wgsl: a depth-guided a-trous pass over the world frame that averages the lighting of terrain whose voxels project smaller than render.denoisePx* pixels (the mid-distance staircase speckle). One terrain view drawn raw and filtered, read back with the depth the world pass wrote, compared by distance band. A: pixels nearer than 10 m and the sky are bit-identical (nearMaxDiff, 0 on purpose: the strength ramp is exactly zero there and the shader returns the source texel). B: in the 30-400 m band the mean absolute residual against the 4-neighbour mean falls to at most midHfMaxRatio of the raw frame's. C: that band's mean luminance moves by at most midMeanMaxDelta (0..255). The *Observed values and the per-frame cost are recorded for --rebaseline.
